penetration_assumption: Each new specialty-flour SKU sells like the AVERAGE OF ARY'S OWN 12 LIVE NON-WHEAT SPECIALTY FLOURS — Rs 2,212 per SKU per year (VERIFIED: ragi 5,910 / jowar 5,744 / bajra 5,125 / samak 3,980 / kuttu 2,850 / jau 650 / sattu 588 / roasted+whole variants = Rs 26,547 across 12 SKUs, live 12m). That is this campus's demonstrated appetite for non-wheat flour, not a borrowed benchmark. 10 credible lines x Rs 2,212 = Rs 22,120/yr revenue, at the VERIFIED retail-tier gross margin of 16.1% = Rs 3,562/yr gross profit. GENEROUS CASE: if new lines do 2x the shelf average because the existing ones are chronically out of stock (Ragi sold in only 5 of 12 months, Kuttu 3 of 12), it is Rs 44,240 revenue / Rs 7,123 GP. Either way it is 0.7-1.3% of a Rs 33.89 L category. I did NOT assume a resident-penetration rate — with 4,700 residents, a Rs 40/kg product and 10 slow flour lines, any "x% of residents buy one pack a month" assumption would have produced a number 10-50x larger than what ARY's own comparable shelf actually does. The comparator is the honest ceiling.
probe_evidence: All 23 "missing" and 3 "dormant" lines were re-probed with `ary assort probe` before being accepted. THIS TIME THE DIFF WAS RIGHT — unlike the earlier passes that produced 81 false missings. Confirmed genuinely absent (probe returned only unrelated name-collisions): sabut gehun/wheat grain (63 matches, ALL Jivo wheatgrass juice + bread + Cerelac, zero grain); high-protein atta (12 matches, all SHAMPOO — Clinic Plus/Dove/Tresemme); diabetic/low-GI atta (0 rows); gluten-free (0 rows); rajgira/amaranth (0 rows); rice flour (4 matches, all "Rajma Chawal/Kadi Chawal" Mini Meals dishes); chana/missi atta (1 match = Bonn Missi BREAD); soya flour (72 matches, all soya OIL + Nutrela chunks, no flour); multi-millet atta (9 matches, all biscuits/bread/muesli); idli rice + idli rava + bansi rava (matched only MTR/Gits instant mixes and Ravalgaon LOLLIPOPS); broken rice (3 matches, all "Tukda" pickle + Shahi Tukda); wheat bran (7 matches, all rice-bran OIL + bran bread); sella/parboiled (0 rows); no pack >=15 kg exists anywhere in staples (only 15 L oil, 15 kg dahi, 15 kg frozen smileys). METHOD WARNING I HIT AND CORRECTED: in zsh an unquoted variable is NOT word-split, so `probe $terms` sends one long string and silently returns 0 matches. That produced four false "0 rows" in my first pass (I nearly filed a tool bug). Verified: `probe fortified` = 2 SKUs but `probe $q` where q="fortified bharat" = 0; `probe ${=q}` = 3. The probe tool's OR logic is correct — always pass terms as separate literal arguments.
kill_reason: The gap is real but trivial; the binding constraint is availability, proved four ways. (1) LISTED-BUT-NEVER-STOCKED: of 242 active SKUs in groups 110+143, only 103 sold in 12m; 8 were stocked and did not sell; 1 has stock with no purchase; and 130 (54%) had ZERO purchase, ZERO stock and ZERO sales in the window. 82 of those never sold a single unit in the database's life (2023->). ARY's real staples range is 112 lines, not 242. (2) ALL THREE "DORMANT" LINES ARE IN THAT NEVER-STOCKED BUCKET, so adding them is worse than useless — they are already listed: Patanjali Fortified Atta 5Kg and 10Kg (never sold, ever), Amul Organic Sona Masoori (last sold 2024-10-21, whole Amul Organic range dead since 2024), Singhara Atta 250 Gm (last sold 2024-10-04 — it sold through one Navratri then was never restocked, through two more). Same for the "missing 1kg branded top-up pack" the demand file calls a leak: Aashirwad Chakki Atta 1 Kg is listed and never stocked. (3) REVENUE CONCENTRATION: 67% of the category (Rs 22,81,892) is ONE customer — "Hunger Heroes" (002CM), a langar/community-kitchen account — on 12 bills, at a VERIFIED 1.3% gross margin costed off the purchase ledger. It bought Rs 69.81 L across all categories on those 12 bills, 9.2% of ARY's whole Rs 7.55 Cr business. Real household retail staples is only Rs 11.07 L (Rs 236/resident/yr) on 9,198 bills at 16.1% GM. (4) THE LEVERS ARE ELSEWHERE: moving the Hunger Heroes contract from 1.3% to 3.0% GM adds Rs 38,792/yr gross profit — 10.9x everything the entire assortment build would earn — with zero new SKUs, zero shelf, zero working capital. Delisting the 82 phantom SKUs and fixing Rajdhani Daliya 1 Kg (VERIFIED selling below cost: Rs 35.14 realised vs Rs 37.33 paid, Rs 7,576/yr loss) are both bigger than the whole gap.
top_skus: Rajgira / amaranth flour 500g — completes the vrat set (VERIFIED vrat cohort Rs 90,276/yr, 11 selling SKUs; kuttu and samak already sell)
Rice flour 500g — Himachali chilra/pathande base; the one absent line with a LOCAL dish behind it rather than a South-Indian one
Chana / missi atta 1kg — traditional diabetic roti, and the only substitute available since no branded diabetic atta exists
Thin / nylon poha 500g — poha is the category's BEST margin at 22.5% VERIFIED (Jadugar 500g); ARY carries one grade only
Multi-millet blend atta 1kg — millet attas ARY already stocks (ragi/bajra/jowar) each sell Rs 5,100-5,900
Fine / chiroti rava 500g — ARY carries one undifferentiated sooji grade (Shakti Bhog, Rs 23,619, sells 12/12 months)
High-protein atta 1kg — one facing only; university/gym cohort, unproven at ARY

Diabetic / sugar-release-control atta 1kg — CAUTION: ARY sells ZERO antidiabetic medicines (probe: metformin/glimepiride/insulin = 0 rows), so this cohort is UNPROVEN here; the campus hospital likely serves it
Soya flour 500g — protein extender; soya sells at ARY only as oil and chunks
Gluten-free atta blend 1kg — lowest confidence of the ten, no demand proxy exists
blockers: Shelf and catalogue hygiene, not space: 130 of 242 active staples SKUs were never stocked in 12m and 82 never sold ever. Adding 10 lines to a catalogue that is already 54% phantom makes the ordering screen worse. DELIST FIRST, then add — otherwise the new lines join the tail.

Hill humidity vs slow flour: Baru Sahib monsoon crosses 80% RH and atta keeps 1-2 months. A 500g specialty flour turning Rs 2,212/yr moves ~4 packs a month — several of these will expire before they sell. This is the main reason the existing specialty shelf looks thin: Ragi sold in 5 of 12 months, Kuttu in 3 of 12.

Supplier reach from Rajgarh HP: rajgira, gluten-free and diabetic atta come via Chandigarh/Solan distributors with case-pack MOQs (typically 10-12 units) that exceed several months of demand at these volumes. MOQ, not capital, is what creates the dead stock.

Capital is NOT a blocker and should not be cited as one: 10 lines at one case each is roughly Rs 15,000-25,000 of stock. That is the point — the opportunity is too small to need a business case, and too small to matter.
Management attention is the real scarce resource. The Hunger Heroes contract (Rs 22.8 L at 1.3% GM) and the 82 phantom listings compete for the same buyer's time and are 10x the value.

NOT a blocker, and worth saying plainly: no licence problem. ARY already sells loose atta/rice by weight (VERIFIED UnitName='Kgs', GST-exempt, IncludeInRate=1), so the FSSAI licence and Legal-Metrology scale the demand research flags as a prerequisite are already in place.

Institutional bags (25-30kg atta/rice/maida) CANNOT be sized as revenue and were excluded: the canteens are internal consumption units, not customers — Ary G Canteen, Ary Apple A Day and Ary Lite show 0 POS sales and 0 purchases, with stock transferred in and booked to Consumption (VERIFIED via Stock.Cons by warehouse). A bulk bag there is a procurement saving of roughly Rs 15,000-19,000/yr (ESTIMATED: ~3,700-4,800 kg/yr of canteen-bound retail packs at a Rs 4/kg bulk spread — the bulk price is NOT-CHECKED, no market source in this DB), never new revenue.

Four lines were dropped as having no demand basis at this campus, not deferred: idli rice, idli rava, bansi/samba rava and fine South-Indian grades — South-Indian food sells almost nothing here (all idli/dosa/sambar items = Rs 8,676/yr). Sprouted-ragi weaning flour was dropped too: the ENTIRE baby cohort is Rs 32,561/yr across 70 SKUs and all 34 Cerelac SKUs together sold Rs 3,878. Bharat/NAFED rice was dropped as a government-scheme SKU not available to a private retailer.
